name: crewdson-terrace-blue-hour
prompt: Every gang member wears a knitted balaclava covering the whole head, with no eye, nose or mouth holes; a large white ring is stitched round the face, and a red triangle sits high over the wearer's left eye (on the right of the picture, at about 2 o'clock); gloves on both hands, collars and cuffs closed, no skin showing anywhere. A staged photographic tableau, tall portrait frame, on an ordinary British street of red-brick Victorian terraced houses at the last minute of dusk. Planted in the middle of the tarmac, between the two rows of houses, rises a single enormous block of stacked white paper, crisp and squared off, as tall as the rooftops and chimney pots, its top edge printed in heavy black capitals: THE RULES. Five gang members stand small in the bottom third of the frame, spaced in a loose uneven row on the road with their backs half turned to us, heads tilted right back to stare up at it; they wear today's clothes: puffer jackets, a zipped tracksuit top, a hooded parka, cargo trousers, trainers; their masks are each a different muted colour. Around them the street is everyday and exact: green and black wheelie bins at the kerb, a silver hatchback and a small red city car parked half on the pavement, a satellite dish, net curtains. Every light in the scene is deliberately placed and switched on: orange sodium streetlamps pooling on wet tarmac, warm yellow glow behind front-room curtains, a dome light left on inside one parked car, and one hard cold white beam from high above the left-hand roofs grazing the face of the paper block so every sheet edge shows. A thin ground mist hangs at kerb height and catches the lamps. The sky above the chimneys is a deep saturated cobalt blue; everything below it is warm amber and sodium orange, the two held in tension. Camera on a tripod at pavement height, a 24mm wide view looking straight down the street, very deep focus with the paper block the sharpest thing in the picture, still and quiet, no motion blur, large-format photographic detail, the mood hushed and unsettling, as if the street is holding its breath.
